newsitem.title: USA: U.S. favors Poland, Czech Republic, Hungary for NATO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. favors Poland, Czech Republic, Hungary for NATO.

text.p: The United States favors only the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to join NATO in the first round of new members invited to enter the security alliance, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday.
"The United States will formally say today that of the candidate members for admission to NATO we will favor in the first round Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary," McCurry told reporters.

"There obviously were other serious candidates -- Romania and Slovenia both are clearly on track -- but in the view of the United States they will profit by having more time to fully develop their capacities within the parameters of the Partnership for Peace Program," McCurry added.
"We do continue to favor an open-door policy with respect to NATO membership and no one should be excluded from consideration and this should not be considered the last round of admissions," he said.

U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen will present the U.S. position on the matter on Thursday in Brussels at a meeting of North Atlantic Treaty Organization defense ministers, McCurry said, adding: "The United States position is firm."

Asked if the United States might be overruled on the matter by other NATO members, McCurry replied: "That is not likely." New members are expected to be formally invited to join the alliance at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.
